text:
Omar El-Sayed: Hit a cherry-pick conflict trying to pull the scheduler fix into `runtime-1.20-lts` (from main). This is the fix for the queue fairness regression (original PR #8417). `rw-backport` got stuck on `scheduler/placement_policy.cc` + `scheduler/queue_state.h`.

Omar El-Sayed: Error from the tool:
```
$ rw-backport --from-pr 8417 --to runtime-1.20-lts --new-pr
...
Cherry-picking 3 commits...
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in scheduler/placement_policy.cc
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in scheduler/queue_state.h
error: could not apply 3c9f2ac scheduler: clamp inflight per tenant to avoid starvation
```
I can resolve manually but want to make sure we keep minimal diff for LTS.

Sofia Ivanova: :eyes: yeah that one touched a bunch of scheduler internals on main after the metrics refactor. What’s the conflict cause—just surrounding code drift or actual behavior differences?

Omar El-Sayed: Mostly drift. On main `QueueState` has the new `InFlightTracker` helper. On 1.20 it’s still `inflight_by_tenant` map + the old mutex.

Omar El-Sayed: In `placement_policy.cc` the conflict is around the selection loop.
On main it’s now:
```
for (auto& candidate : candidates) {
  auto inflight = state.inflight_tracker().ForTenant(tid);
  ...
}
```
On LTS branch it’s:
```
auto it = state.inflight_by_tenant.find(tid);
...
```
The actual fix we need is the clamp + tie-breaker so a single tenant can’t pin the whole batch.

Samir Qureshi: We should avoid backporting the refactor (tracker + helper methods). For LTS, I’d prefer we implement the clamp in terms of existing fields even if it’s slightly uglier.

Kira Volkov: +1 minimal-diff. If we port the helper we’ll pull in unrelated header changes + tests, and our CI matrix for LTS will light up.

Connor O'Brien: Agree. LTS backport bar is “surgical patch”, not “make branches match.” If it’s 2-3 hunks, do it by hand and add a note in the backport PR description about why we didn’t include the tracker refactor.

Sahana Iyer: Also: please don’t resolve by wholesale taking main’s file. The determinism check in LTS CI will flag big diffs sometimes (line endings + formatting changes) and it makes review painful.

Hiro Tanaka: Any perf impact? That fix changes scheduling decisions. If we do a minimal implementation, we should keep the same algorithmic complexity as 1.20, not add extra map lookups in the inner loop.

Sofia Ivanova: Omar can you paste the actual conflicting hunk? Might be we can just add the clamp right before computing the score.

Omar El-Sayed: Here’s the conflict hunk in `placement_policy.cc`:
```
<<<<<<< HEAD
  // old code: score is basically (available - inflight)
  const int inflight = state.InFlightForTenant(tenant_id);
  score = available_tokens - inflight;
=======
  // new code: cap inflight contribution to avoid starvation
  const int inflight = state.inflight_tracker().ForTenant(tenant_id);
  const int capped = std::min(inflight, cfg.max_inflight_per_tenant_cap);
  score = available_tokens - capped;
>>>>>>> 3c9f2ac
```
In LTS we don’t have `cfg.max_inflight_per_tenant_cap` either (config field added later). On main it defaults to 128.

Samir Qureshi: Then LTS strategy:
1) hardcode cap constant for LTS (ideally via an existing config knob?)
2) keep function signature the same
3) add a comment “LTS-only clamp; see PR #8417 for mainline config support”

Sofia Ivanova: We should *not* hardcode if we can avoid it. Is there an existing knob in 1.20 config that approximates this? Maybe `max_concurrent_requests_per_tenant`?

Omar El-Sayed: There’s `tenant_max_inflight` but it’s a strict admission limit, not a scoring cap. The bug is that under bursty load, even under the limit, one tenant’s inflight dominates scoring and they keep getting picked.

Kira Volkov: If we introduce a new config field to 1.20-lts we’re expanding surface area. That’s probably worse than a constant, tbh.

Connor O'Brien: For LTS I’d accept a constant if it’s clearly documented + low risk. But we should pick something conservative and align with main default (128) unless there’s reason not to.

Hiro Tanaka: 128 is fine. It caps the penalty, it doesn’t raise throughput by itself. The risk is fairness behavior changes, but that’s the point.

Sofia Ivanova: Ok. Let’s implement cap = 128 in the scoring path only. Don’t change admission control. Also add a regression test if 1.20 has the scheduler fairness test harness.

Omar El-Sayed: There is `scheduler/tests/test_fairness.cc` but it’s pretty coarse. We can add a unit that constructs two tenants with skewed inflight and ensures selection rotates.

Sahana Iyer: Please keep test deterministic; avoid timing-based assertions. Our LTS CI is slower.

Samir Qureshi: Another option is to cherry-pick only the first commit (the clamp) and skip the later commit that “renames metrics fields” which is probably what’s causing the second conflict.

Omar El-Sayed: The 3 commits are:
- A) clamp inflight contribution
- B) add config knob + plumb to runtime config
- C) update scheduler metrics label
We want A only. `rw-backport` is trying to pick all 3 because they’re in the PR.

Connor O'Brien: Then do it manually:
- `git cherry-pick -n <commitA>`
- resolve conflicts
- commit with message `Backport: <hash> (PR #8417)`
- and in the backport PR, link to original PR and state “partial backport; omitted config + metrics changes”.

Omar El-Sayed: yup. I’ll abort current cherry-pick and do that.

github-bot: Omar El-Sayed pushed a commit to redwood/runtime-1.20-lts: `f1b7a02` (wip) (link)

Omar El-Sayed: New attempt:
```
$ git cherry-pick --abort
$ git cherry-pick -n 3c9f2ac
# resolve
$ git status
  both modified: scheduler/placement_policy.cc
  both modified: scheduler/queue_state.h
```
`queue_state.h` conflict is just function name mismatch (`InFlightForTenant` signature changed on main).

Sofia Ivanova: In 1.20 `InFlightForTenant(tid)` returns `int` already right? then no need to touch `queue_state.h` beyond context.

Omar El-Sayed: Correct. I resolved `queue_state.h` by leaving it unchanged. In `placement_policy.cc` I added:
```
constexpr int kInflightScoreCap = 128;
...
const int inflight = state.InFlightForTenant(tenant_id);
const int capped = std::min(inflight, kInflightScoreCap);
score = available_tokens - capped;
```
And comment:
`// LTS: clamp inflight penalty to avoid tenant starvation (see mainline PR #8417)`

Hiro Tanaka: Good. Where did you put the constexpr? File scope is fine, but avoid polluting headers.

Omar El-Sayed: File scope in `placement_policy.cc`.

Kira Volkov: Can we add a small test in `test_fairness.cc` that asserts the starved tenant gets scheduled within N iterations? Like build a fake candidate list and call `SelectNextTenant()` repeatedly.

Samir Qureshi: As long as it doesn’t rely on wall clock. Use fixed seeds.

Omar El-Sayed: Added a unit test `FairnessClampPreventsStarvation` that runs 100 selections and expects tenant B scheduled at least once when tenant A inflight is huge. It’s deterministic because the candidate ordering is stable.

Sahana Iyer: Make sure it doesn’t depend on hash map iteration order. Use vectors.

Omar El-Sayed: Good catch—switching to vector, no unordered_map iteration.

Connor O'Brien: What’s the diff size now?

Omar El-Sayed: `git diff --stat`:
- `scheduler/placement_policy.cc | 14 ++++++++++----`
- `scheduler/tests/test_fairness.cc | 28 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++`
No other files.

Sofia Ivanova: That’s LTS-appropriate.

Omar El-Sayed: Opening backport PR now. Labels: `needs-backport` is already on the original, but for this PR I’ll add `backport-runtime-1.20-lts` + `backport-risk-low`.

Connor O'Brien: Add `release-note-lts` too so changelog generator picks it up.

Omar El-Sayed: done.

Hiro Tanaka: Before merge, please run the scheduler microbench locally (or kick the perf-canary dry run) just to ensure the extra `std::min` doesn’t show up in hot path. Should be negligible but let’s be safe.

Omar El-Sayed: I ran `bazel test //scheduler/tests:test_fairness` and `//scheduler/tests:test_scheduler_unit`. Green.
I can trigger perf-canary on the PR once it’s up.

Sofia Ivanova: Also mention in PR description: “Behavior change: more fairness across tenants; may change tail latency distribution slightly under multi-tenant saturation.” Ops will ask.

Omar El-Sayed: Will do.

Kira Volkov: :thumbsup: This is exactly the “minimal diff backport” pattern we want for LTS. If review goes smooth, we can cite it as an example in the backport policy doc.

Connor O'Brien: +1. Link me the PR when ready.

Omar El-Sayed: PR is up: #8521 (runtime-1.20-lts) — “LTS backport: clamp inflight penalty to avoid tenant starvation (partial backport of #8417)”.

Sahana Iyer: Watching CI. If the determinism job complains about the constexpr placement (it sometimes flags compile flags differences), we’ll adjust.

Samir Qureshi: Thanks. I’ll review for correctness + ensure we didn’t accidentally change locking semantics.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll take the scheduler logic review.

Connor O'Brien: Once it’s approved, we’ll slot it into the next RC. Please add the Linear link in the PR body too (ENG-4823 or whatever is tracking).

Omar El-Sayed: Added ENG-4823 + SUP-3950 references in the PR body. End of thread for now unless CI breaks.
